newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close firmer after Dow rebound.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close firmer after Dow rebound.

text.p: Australian shares closed firmer on moderate volume on Tuesday as investors factored in the strong recovery of the U.S. market.
The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, ended 22 points higher at 2,361.8, close to its intra-session high of 2,364.3.
Brokers said the market's gain was slightly disappointing given the Dow's 82 point surge on Monday and the 2.9 percent fall the Australian market suffered on Friday.

"There has been some quite large lines go through in some stocks which suggests people are happy to take big positions now but the volume generally was not extremely high," said Nick Atkinson, a dealer at Brisbane broker Wilson HTM.

Banks dominated buying activity with ANZ and National Australia topping the value turnover list. The stock of media group News Corp was also favoured by local investors after its ADRs were supported in New York on Monday.
Dealers said despite the rise investors remained cautious with the principal concern being the inexorable rise of the Wall Street market.
"When the market falls 70 points people get a bit bruised and battered and a little bit tentative. They have their feelers out and are just taking bites here and there," Atkinson said.
One issue out of step with the market was beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil whose shares continued their recent downward move following a profit downgrade in mid-November.
Coca-Cola Amatil shares closed 20 cents weaker at A$13.10 (US$10.48).
